issue.title: Scoped check never selects the agent-artifact marker AST audits, so marker-writer changes land deterministic Master Gate reds

task_type_fields.impact:
Any agent that changes a done.json/agent_meta.json/running.json/waiting.json writer passes its scoped check and lands a deterministic red on master. The red surfaces only in Master Gate and Full CI. Here that blocked the sase v0.18.0 release for a full Full CI cycle (~1.5 h per leg) and needed a nested repair epic.

The contract set has a 30 s serial budget (tests/test_contract_manifest.py), and these audits currently cost ~24 s of setup (full AST scan of src/sase). So plain contract admission is not viable. A fix likely needs one of two things. Option 1 is a cheap substring pre-filter on the tracked marker literals, like the commit-tag contract's `"commit"` pre-filter (8.6 s to 0.46 s), followed by contract admission within budget. Option 2 is a path-based broadening rule that selects the marker audits when a changed `src/sase` file contains a tracked marker literal. Do not loosen the audits themselves.
task_type_fields.repro:
Found by the sase-1mk.9 land agent while root-causing why a release epic's own commit turned every Master Gate and Full CI red.

Phase sase-1mk.9.5 committed e5c02dc8a4. It changed `src/sase/axe/run_agent_exec_markers.py:write_done_marker_and_update_index` and `src/sase/axe/run_agent_runner_finalize.py:write_error_done_marker` to write `done.json` through `write_json_marker_atomic`. Its scoped `sase tool run check` (ToolRun a5b7bf5d2604abf8e656331d6b01d02f) selected 523/5274 test files and passed. It never selected `tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_mutation_audit.py` or `tests/test_agent_artifact_marker_path_passing_audit.py`.

Those two AST audits deterministically fail 4 nodes on that change. They failed in Master Gate 39169961708 shards 6/7 and in every later Master Gate and Full CI test leg (task sase-1mt). The cause: the audits read `src/sase/**` as text through `tests/_agent_artifact_marker_audit_helpers.py`, so the import graph in `tests/_test_selection.py` gives them no edge to the modules they audit. They are also not in the curated `contract` set (`tests/contract_manifest.txt`, marker `pytest.mark.contract`).

Repro: on a tree that edits only a tracked-marker writer under `src/sase/axe/`, run `tools/select_tests` (or `sase tool run check`). Neither marker audit module is selected.

issue.creation_reason: A release-epic phase's scoped check passed while its change deterministically broke the marker audits in every Master Gate and Full CI leg. The selection gap predates that epic and will recur for any marker-writer change.

payload.description: sase-1mt is the marker-audit catalog drift that slipped through this selection gap
Check overlap/name collision with PyPI E3 trustworthy-signal epic

payload.entry: Fixed by epic sase-1pu phase sase-1pu.3, commit fd8882c6af. RULE_MARKER_AUDIT in tests/_test_selection_rules.py is wired into select_tests in tests/_test_selection.py. It adds both marker AST audits whenever a changed src/*.py file contains a tracked marker literal. The literal catalog is imported from tests/_agent_artifact_marker_audit_helpers, so the rule cannot drift from the audits. The audits and the contract budget are unchanged. The fallout from that import (missing helper in the scoped miniature repo) was fixed by 86bec79ca4. The sase-1pu lander reran tests/test_test_selection_marker_audits.py (4 tests), both audits, tests/test_contract_manifest.py, and tests/test_suite_gate_scoped_integration.py on master 71827cfecc: all passed.
